mainTopic: Why one תנא can use ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ to teach that one placement of blood is enough, while other teachings that seem to need the same פסוק come from other sources or other views.
overview: Just before this, a תנא learned from ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ (דברים 12:27) that one placement of blood is enough. The גמרא challenges this three times, each time saying the פסוק is needed for something else. First, the rule that leftover blood goes on the יסוד: this תנא learns that from רבי's reading of the extra word ״בַּדָּם״. Second, the rule that pouring works for blood meant to be thrown: this תנא holds like רבי עקיבא, who keeps throwing and pouring separate, as shown from the משנה about the ברכות on the פסח and the זבח. Third, רבי ישמעאל's rule that מעשר and פסח need blood and fats on the מזבח: this תנא holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי, who learns that from the plural words ״דָּמָם״ and ״חֶלְבָּם״. The גמרא then asks how רבי ישמעאל can use one פסוק twice, and answers that two תנאים report his view differently. Finally it asks how רבי יוסי הגלילי explains ״וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ״, since the owners eat מעשר and פסח. The answer is that the plural means an unblemished בכור and a blemished one.

steps.title: Isn't this verse needed for the base rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a teaching that uses ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ to show that all blood needs to be placed on the יסוד. This challenges the תנא who used the same פסוק to teach that one placement is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that all blood needs to be placed on the base of the altar? The verse says: "And the blood of your offerings shall be poured."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a teaching that uses the same פסוק for a different rule: all leftover blood goes on the base of the מזבח. If the פסוק is busy teaching that, how can the earlier תנא use it to teach that one placement is enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single פסוק is normally not used for two separate rules unless there is a reason. The earlier תנא read ״יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ as teaching that one placement is enough. This teaching reads the same word as sending leftover blood to the יסוד, so the two uses seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we know)? It asks for the source of a rule.
The base of the outer מזבח, where leftover blood is poured.
Placing of blood on the מזבח.
The verse says. It introduces the source פסוק.

steps.confusionAlert: This line looks like a calm question, but in context it is a challenge to the earlier תנא. That is why the next step answers it by finding a different source.

phrases.english: From where do we know, for all the bloods,
that they require placing blood on the base?
phrases.notes: This means the leftover blood that remains after the main placements.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And the blood of your offerings shall be poured."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְכׇל הַדָּמִים שֶׁטְּעוּנִים מַתַּן דָּם לַיְסוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier use, just before this, of ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ to teach that one placement is enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier תנא's reading of ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ as teaching that one placement is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already being used to teach that all blood goes on the יסוד, so it seems unavailable for another rule.

steps.title: He learns the base rule from רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this תנא gets the יסוד rule from a different source: the teaching of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns that rule from רבי's teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the earlier תנא learns the base rule from a different פסוק, the one רבי uses. This line sets up the ברייתא of רבי that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the יסוד rule has another source, ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ is free. It can teach that one placement is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it (from another source).

phrases.english: He derives it from Rabbi's teaching.
phrases.notes: "He" is the earlier תנא who used the פסוק for one placement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 by pointing to a different source for the יסוד rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate source: the rule comes from a different פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only source for the יסוד rule is ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״.
steps.terutzMaskana: The יסוד rule comes from רבי's reading of ״וְהַנִּשְׁאָר בַּדָּם יִמָּצֵה״, so the פסוק in דברים is free.

steps.title: רבי notices an extra word in the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי's ברייתא. רבי points out that the word ״בַּדָּם״ in ״וְהַנִּשְׁאָר בַּדָּם יִמָּצֵה״ seems unneeded and asks why it is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says: "And the rest of the blood shall be squeezed out." The verse did not need to say "of the blood." So why does it say "of the blood"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for its answer: a ברייתא from רבי. Here רבי only asks his question about the extra word, which sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about a bird חטאת, and the whole פסוק already talks about blood. So the word ״בַּדָּם״ looks extra, and an extra word in the תורה is a sign of an added teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: And the rest (the leftover).
Shall be squeezed out (drained).
Why does the verse say this? It points to an extra word.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi says:
"And the rest of the blood shall be squeezed out"
since the verse did not need to say "of the blood";
so why does the verse say "of the blood"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that step 2 pointed to.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 2 that the יסוד rule has a separate source.

steps.title: The extra word covers all offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains that we already knew the base rule only for offerings with four placements. The extra word ״בַּדָּם״ extends it to all blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we only learned about offerings placed with four placements that their blood requires the base. From where do we know it for other bloods? The verse says: "And the rest of the blood shall be squeezed out." The verse did not need to say "of the blood," so why does it say "of the blood"? It teaches that all bloods require placement on the base.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers his own question: the extra word ״בַּדָּם״ teaches that every offering's leftover blood goes on the יסוד, not only the four-placement offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was already known for offerings with four placements, meaning the outer חטאת. The extra word stretches the rule to all other offerings. This finishes the answer to step 1, because the יסוד rule now has its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: Four placements: blood put on the four corners of the מזבח.
The other bloods (other offerings).
It taught. It introduces the lesson of the extra word.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that all leftover blood goes on the יסוד comes from the extra word ״בַּדָּם״ in ויקרא 5:9, according to רבי.

phrases.english: Because we have only learned
about those placed with four placements
phrases.notes: These are the outer חטאת offerings, whose blood goes on all four corners.

phrases.english: that they require placing the blood on the base;
for other bloods, from where do we know?
The verse says: "And the rest of the blood shall be squeezed out"
since the verse did not need to say "of the blood";
so why does the verse say "of the blood"?
It teaches about all the bloods
that they require placing the blood on the base.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא לָמַדְנוּ אֶלָּא לַנִּיתָּנִין מַתַּן אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the extra word that רבי raised in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק includes the extra word ״בַּדָּם״.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It extends the יסוד requirement from four-placement offerings to all offerings.

steps.title: The verse is needed for pouring instead of throwing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ is needed for another teaching: blood that should be thrown still counts if it was poured.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, does the verse come for this? He needs it for what was taught: From where do we know that blood meant to be placed by throwing, if he placed it by pouring, he has fulfilled his duty? The verse says: "And the blood of your offerings shall be poured."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge against using the פסוק for the one-placement rule. A ברייתא already uses it to teach that pouring works for blood that was supposed to be thrown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יסוד rule was moved to another source, but the פסוק still seems busy. Another ברייתא reads ״יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ ("poured") as saying that pouring is acceptable even where throwing was required. So the one-placement teaching seems to have no room.

keyTerms.meaning: But still. It opens a new challenge after an answer.
He needs it (for something else).
Throwing: the blood is thrown at the מזבח from a distance.
Pouring: the blood is poured from close up.
He has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.english: But still, does it come for this?!
phrases.notes: "It" is ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״, and "this" is the rule that one placement is enough.

phrases.english: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא:
From where do we know, regarding blood that is placed by throwing,
that if he placed it by pouring, he has fulfilled his duty?
The verse says: "And the blood of your offerings shall be poured."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 4 frees the פסוק from the יסוד rule, this step finds another use that seems to block it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ to teach that one placement is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is needed to teach that pouring is valid for blood meant to be thrown, so it is not free for another rule.

steps.title: He follows רבי עקיבא: throwing and pouring are separate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this תנא holds like רבי עקיבא. For him, throwing and pouring are separate actions, so he does not learn that pouring works where throwing was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי עקיבא, who says: throwing is not included in pouring, and pouring is not included in throwing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. This תנא follows רבי עקיבא, so the "pouring works for throwing" teaching is not his view, and the פסוק is free for the one-placement rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that throwing and pouring are two different actions, and neither one counts in place of the other. So for him ״יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ cannot teach that pouring works for blood meant to be thrown. That leaves the פסוק available to teach that one placement is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (follows the view of).
Included within.

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא who learns from ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ that one placement is enough does so because he gets the יסוד rule from רבי, and because he holds like רבי עקיבא that throwing and pouring are separate.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a תנא's view on one question (whether pouring can count as throwing) decides which teachings a פסוק is free to give.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Akiva, who says:
Throwing is not included in pouring,
and pouring is not included in throwing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by tying this תנא to רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaitic dispute: the conflicting teaching belongs to a different view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone holds that ״יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ teaches that pouring works for blood meant to be thrown.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי עקיבא, throwing and pouring are separate actions, so the פסוק is free to teach that one placement is enough.

steps.title: Proof that רבי עקיבא keeps throwing and pouring separate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about the ברכה on the פסח and the זבח. רבי ישמעאל says one ברכה can cover the other in one direction. רבי עקיבא says neither ברכה covers the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone said the ברכה over the פסח, he does not need a separate ברכה over the זבח. If he said the ברכה over the זבח, he still needs one over the פסח. This is what רבי ישמעאל says. רבי עקיבא says: neither ברכה covers the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its last answer. It shows from a משנה that רבי עקיבא really does see throwing and pouring as two separate things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of the פסח is poured, and the blood of the זבח that comes with it is thrown. רבי ישמעאל holds that pouring includes throwing, so the פסח ברכה covers the זבח. רבי עקיבא holds that the two never cover each other, which shows he treats them as fully separate actions.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempted; one ברכה takes care of the other, so no second ברכה is needed
The ברכה said before eating the קרבן פסח
Here, the חגיגה (holiday שלמים) eaten together with the פסח
This one does not exempt that one; each needs its own ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about ברכות, not about blood. The גמרא uses it because the reason behind the מחלוקת is whether pouring and throwing count as the same kind of action.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: If he said the blessing over the פסח,
he has exempted the blessing of the זבח.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל זֶבַח – לֹא פָּטַר אֶת הַפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: If he said the one of the זבח, he has not exempted the פסח.
These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
רבי עקיבא says:
This one does not exempt that one,
and that one does not exempt this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 6 by showing a source where רבי עקיבא holds that throwing and pouring are separate.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי עקיבא treats זריקה and שפיכה as separate actions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פסחים about whether the ברכה on the פסח covers the זבח and the other way around.

steps.title: Is the פסוק really free to teach this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ is already needed for a different teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Still, does this פסוק really come for this? It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attack on using ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ for our rule. It is setting up the ברייתא it will quote next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after we said this תנא holds like רבי עקיבא, the פסוק still may not be free. If the פסוק is busy teaching something else, it cannot also be the source for our rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Still; even after the last answer
Does it come for this purpose?
It is needed for something else
For what was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Still, does it come for this?!
phrases.notes: "It" is the פסוק ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ from the last few steps.

phrases.english: It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 6 removed one competing use of the פסוק, this step raises another competing use.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ as the source for our rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק that is already needed for one teaching is not free to teach a second one.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's ברייתא: מעשר and פסח need blood on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learns from a פסוק that a בכור needs its blood and fats on the מזבח. He uses ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ to teach the same for מעשר and פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: Since it says, "But the firstborn of an ox, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat...", we learned that a בכור needs its blood and its fats put on the מזבח. Where do we learn this for מעשר and פסח? The פסוק says: "And the blood of your offerings shall be poured."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that proves its challenge. Here רבי ישמעאל already uses ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a בכור, the תורה says clearly that its blood and fats go on the מזבח. For מעשר and פסח, there is no such clear פסוק, so רבי ישמעאל uses ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ for them. That means this פסוק is already busy, which is the problem the גמרא raised in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, brought as a קרבן
Putting the blood on the מזבח
The fats and parts of the animal burned on the מזבח
Here, מעשר בהמה, the tenth animal brought as a קרבן
The פסוק teaches us

phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל says:
Since it is said,
"But the firstborn of an ox, or the firstborn of a sheep,
or the firstborn of a goat, etc."
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says to throw their blood on the מזבח and burn their fats.

phrases.english: we learned about a בכור
that it needs placing of its blood and its fats
on the מזבח.
From where do we know this for מעשר and פסח?
The פסוק teaches:
"And the blood of your offerings shall be poured."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא that Step 8 said already uses the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in Step 8 that ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ is already needed for another lesson.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ישמעאל's ברייתא, which uses the פסוק to teach that מעשר and פסח need blood and fats on the מזבח.
steps.whatToRemember: At this point ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ seems busy teaching that מעשר and פסח, like בכור, need their blood and fats on the מזבח. The next step answers this.

steps.title: The earlier תנא holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The תנא who uses ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ to teach that one placement is enough holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי. For him, the פסוק is not needed for מעשר and פסח, so it is free.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Steps 8–9. The earlier תנא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, not רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ is already used to teach about מעשר and פסח. That is only true for רבי ישמעאל. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns מעשר and פסח from a different פסוק, so for him ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ״ is still free to teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this view)

phrases.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
phrases.notes: "He" is the תנא who learned from ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ that one placement is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Steps 8–9 by giving the earlier תנא a different position.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the earlier view to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ was already used up for מעשר and פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי הגלילי that law comes from somewhere else, so the פסוק is free.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the plural words ״דָּמָם״ and ״חֶלְבָּם״
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the plural wording in the בכור פסוק that בכור, מעשר and פסח all need their blood and fats on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: The פסוק does not say "its blood" but "their blood". It does not say "its fat" but "their fat". This teaches that a בכור, מעשר and פסח all need their blood and their fats to be put on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where רבי יוסי הגלילי gets the law about מעשר and פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a בכור uses plural words: ״דָּמָם״ and ״חֶלְבָּם״. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the plural adds two more offerings, מעשר and פסח. Since he learns this from here, he does not need ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Their blood / their fat (plural words)
Firstborn animal, which is brought as a קרבן
The animal tithe offering
Putting the blood on the מזבח
The fats and parts that are burned on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי ישמעאל can disagree about what ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ teaches. Each one learns מעשר and פסח from a different פסוק.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
"Its blood" is not stated, but rather "their blood";
"Its fat" is not stated, but rather "their fat";
This teaches about a firstborn, the animal tithe and the Pesach offering,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁטָּעוּן מַתַּן דָּמִים וְאֵימוּרִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: that each needs its blood and its sacrificial parts placed on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up Step 10 by showing where רבי יוסי הגלילי learns this law.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי הגלילי does not need ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ for מעשר and פסח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads the plural words in במדבר 18:17

steps.title: Can רבי ישמעאל learn two things from one פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי ישמעאל can use ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ both for pouring and for מעשר and פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל: does he take this one פסוק for this teaching and also for that teaching?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem. רבי ישמעאל seems to use the same פסוק for two different teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 5 used ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ to teach that pouring counts for blood meant to be thrown. That follows רבי ישמעאל, who holds that pouring includes throwing (Step 7). Yet in Step 9, רבי ישמעאל uses the same פסוק to teach about מעשר and פסח. One פסוק usually cannot be used up for both.

keyTerms.meaning: He takes it out (learns it) from
For this (teaching)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael, this verse,
phrases.notes: This is ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״, the פסוק from the earlier steps.

phrases.aramaic: מַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לְהָכִי וּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לְהָכִי?!
phrases.english: does he use it for this and also use it for that?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל – הַאי קְרָא, מַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לְהָכִי וּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לְהָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to רבי ישמעאל and points out a double use of one פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's use of ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק cannot be fully used for two separate teachings at the same time.

steps.title: Two תנאים report רבי ישמעאל differently
steps.stepSummary: Two תנאים each give a different version of what רבי ישמעאל learned from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and each gives his own view of what רבי ישמעאל held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that it is not one person learning two things. Two different תנאים each say רבי ישמעאל used the פסוק in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One תנא says רבי ישמעאל used the פסוק for pouring. The other תנא says he used it for מעשר and פסח. So no single opinion uses the פסוק twice.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים
According to the view of

phrases.english: There are two tanna'im, each with his own version of Rabbi Yishmael's view.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the view between two reports of one תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל uses one פסוק for two teachings.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each teaching comes from a different תנא's report of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatToRemember: No one uses ״וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ״ twice. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns מעשר and פסח from ״דָּמָם״, and two תנאים give two versions of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: ״וּבְשָׂרָם״ fits רבי ישמעאל's reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new question. For רבי ישמעאל, who reads the whole פסוק as being about a בכור, the plural ״וּבְשָׂרָם״ makes good sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי ישמעאל, who reads the entire פסוק as being about a בכור. That is why it is written: "And their meat shall be yours."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. First it shows that the next פסוק fits רבי ישמעאל well. The challenge to רבי יוסי הגלילי comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the plural words in the פסוק refer only to different kinds of בכור. So "their meat goes to the כהן" fits perfectly. This "בשלמא" is preparing a challenge: for רבי יוסי הגלילי, "their" would also include מעשר and פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for... (sets up a coming challenge)
He sets it (reads it) as being about
"And their meat shall be yours" (given to the כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the end of the discussion. ״בִּשְׁלָמָא״ only says what works for one side. The real question, against רבי יוסי הגלילי, comes right after this.

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Yishmael,
who reads the entire verse as being about a firstborn,
that is why it is written: "And their meat shall be yours."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge about how רבי יוסי הגלילי reads the next פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading of the plural words as including מעשר and פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If "their" includes מעשר and פסח, then ״וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ״ would give their meat to the כהן too. Step 15 finishes this challenge.

steps.title: For רבי יוסי, whose meat goes to the כהן?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads the פסוק as also covering מעשר and פסח. But the owners eat those, so the plural ״וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ״, which gives meat to the כהן, is hard to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רבי יוסי, who also applies the פסוק to מעשר and פסח, there is a problem: the owners eat מעשר and פסח. So what does 'and their meat shall be yours' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the question it began in step 14. The plural 'their meat' works for רבי ישמעאל, but it seems not to work for רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ״ are said to the כהן, so the meat belongs to him. A בכור is eaten by the כהן, but מעשר and פסח are eaten by their owners. If רבי יוסי says 'their' covers מעשר and פסח, the פסוק would be wrongly giving their meat to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: He applies it to, he reads the פסוק as talking about
Animal tithe: every tenth animal, brought as a קרבן
The owners of the קרבן
'And their meat shall be yours', the meat goes to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the blood and fats. רבי יוסי already learned from this פסוק that those go on the מזבח for all three. The question is only about the later words that give the meat to the כהן.

phrases.english: But according to רבי יוסי,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי הגלילי from the ברייתא in step 11.

phrases.english: who applies it also to מעשר and פסח –
מעשר and פסח are eaten by the owners;
what is 'and their meat shall be yours'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast set up in step 14: the plural fits easily for רבי ישמעאל, but it is a problem for רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading that the plural בכור פסוק includes מעשר and פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק gives 'their meat' to the כהן, but מעשר and פסח are eaten by their owners, so 'their' cannot refer to them.

steps.title: The plural means two kinds of בכור
steps.stepSummary: The plural ״וּבְשָׂרָם״ is not about מעשר and פסח. It covers two kinds of בכור: one without a blemish and one with a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means both an animal without a blemish and an animal with a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'their meat' refers to two kinds of בכור, not to מעשר and פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור with no blemish is brought as a קרבן, and a blemished בכור is not offered on the מזבח. In both cases the meat belongs to the כהן. So רבי יוסי can learn מעשר and פסח from the earlier plural words, while 'their meat' still talks only about the two kinds of בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with no blemish, fit to be a קרבן
An animal with a blemish, not offered on the מזבח
Both this one and that one

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, the plural words about blood and fats include מעשר and פסח. The plural ״וּבְשָׂרָם״ means a blemished and an unblemished בכור, and both go to the כהן.

phrases.english: both an unblemished one and a blemished one;
phrases.notes: Both are kinds of בכור. That is why the plural fits even though מעשר and פסח are not meant here.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which items the plural word refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Their meat' refers to the same group as the earlier plural words: בכור, מעשר and פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Their meat' refers only to two kinds of בכור, an unblemished one and a blemished one, and both belong to the כהן.
